title: HERO: Preserving Structure and Semantics in Heterogeneous Continual Graph Learning
abstract: arXiv:2505.17458v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Machine learning on heterogeneous graphs has advanced rapidly, driven by the diverse entities, relations, and semantics inherent in real-world data. However, most existing studies assume static graphs, whereas real-world graph data are often continuously updated. Continual learning in this setting is particularly challenging because historical knowledge is encoded not only in target-node representations, but also in their heterogeneous structural contexts and relation-dependent semantic responses. To this end, we introduce HERO, a heterogeneous continual graph learning framework that preserves historical knowledge at both structural and semantic levels while adapting to incoming tasks. We analyze experience replay as an approximation to the unavailable historical gradient and decompose its error into target-selection and context-reconstruction terms. translated_title: HERO：在异构持续图学习中保持结构与语义
translated_abstract: 受现实世界数据中固有的多样实体、关系和语义的驱动，异构图上的机器学习发展迅速。然而，大多数现有研究假设图是静态的，而现实世界的图数据往往是持续更新的。这种设定下的持续学习尤其具有挑战性，因为历史知识不仅编码在目标节点的表示中，还编码在其异构的结构上下文和依赖关系的语义响应中。为此，我们提出了HERO，一个异构持续图学习框架，它在适应新任务的同时，在结构和语义两个层面上保存历史知识。我们将经验重放分析为对不可获取的历史梯度的近似，并将其误差分解为目标选择项和上下文重构项。这一分析表明，仅重放目标节点通常不足以……（摘要内容不完整，此处为原文截断处）
tldr: 该论文提出了HERO框架，通过将经验重放的误差分解为目标选择与上下文重构两部分，证明了仅重放目标节点是不够的，从而在异构持续图学习中同时从结构和语义两个层面保存历史知识。
en_tdlr: HERO is a heterogeneous continual graph learning framework that preserves historical knowledge at both structural and semantic levels, based on an analysis that decomposes experience replay error into target-selection and context-reconstruction terms, showing that replaying target nodes alone is insufficient.
